content:
we've been thinking about the right design for a coalgebra/bialgebra/Hopf algebras quotient API in #39790 and it surfaced some questions that would be helpful to get input on. there are three relevant types in mathlib (RingQuot, RingCon.Quotient, and Ideal.Quotient). so you have three plausible predicates:

  • Bialgebra.IsBialgebraRel R r -> Bialgebra R (RingQuot r)
  • Bialgebra.IsBialgebraCon R c -> Bialgebra R c.Quotient
  • IsBialgebraIdeal R I [I.IsTwoSided] -> Bialgebra R (A ⧸ I)

do we want to support all three? or to make one (RingQuot) primary and bridge? what's the long-term movement in mathlib for quotient carriers?
In general, there are too many quotient type in core + mathlib to my taste. IMO there should be a single quotient type up to syntactic equality
should i have posted this as a broader question in #mathlib4 ? i'm not sure if things get stranded in the PR reviews.
Yes, the issue that you should raise is that there are several ways to quotient a ring (I count 4 at least?) and you don't know which to use
